text:
Amanda: Heads up — saw enforcement spike denies for a few orgs ~08:10UTC, but metering pipeline shows a large batch arriving ~08:11. Suspect late-arriving usage causing false positives when enforcer checks counters.
Josh: which orgs? any request IDs to look at?
Amanda: org-7f9, org-3b2. sample enforcer log snippet: `enforcer: deny org=org-7f9 key=sk-abc reason=quota_exceeded window=60s count=0 burst_allowed=50` followed a minute later by meter pipeline: `aggregator: flushed 23k tokens org=org-7f9`.
Priya: most likely kafka consumer lag + occasional connector retries causing aggregator to flush big batches late. enforcement reads Redis counters with per-window TTL and makes decisions in realtime -> late increments arrive after enforcement already enforced.
Linus: options: 1) make enforcement consult a short 'pending' buffer (pending increments topic / memcache) before denying, 2) bias enforcement towards permissive when metering lag > X, or 3) make aggregator do smoother flushes.
Carlo: prefer 2 + 3. Implement temporary adaptive-bursting when telemetry shows ingestion lag. e.g. config: `adaptive_throttle: {lag_threshold_ms: 30000, extra_burst_pct: 50, evaluation_window_s: 60}`. If lag > 30s, increase burst allowance by 50% for affected keys for the next window.
Emma: +1 for adaptive. but we need strict guardrails so we don't let abuse through. require whitelisted routes and add an emergency budget cap per org.
Priya: also need reconciliation path for orgs that were incorrectly blocked earlier. plan: backfill processed events, compute delta per window, and apply `redis.INCRBY(key, delta)` with the original window timestamp so enforcer's counters reflect true usage. then remove from blocked-set.
Josh: is it safe to tamper with counters retroactively? race conditions with current window. maybe perform backfill-only for windows that are closed (i.e., timestamp < now - enforcement_grace).
Amanda: yes, do backfill only for closed windows. enforcement_grace could be `2 * flush_interval`. We'll mark backfilled windows in a reconciliation index so we don't double-apply.
Linus: sample reconcile pseudo: ```
// for each org,window where events_arrived_late:
delta = sum(tokens_in_events) - recorded_count(window)
if window_is_closed:
  redis.hincrby(counter_key, window_ts, delta)
  mark_reconciled(org, window_ts)
```
Carlo: alerting/observability: add PromQLs. Example: `sum(increase(meter_flushed_events[1m])) by (org)` vs `sum(increase(enforcer_check_count{decision="deny"}[1m])) by (org)` and an alert when flushed_events >> enforcer_denies and consumer_lag > X.
Emma: dashboard tiles: consumer_lag_histogram, enforcer_deny_rate, blocked_org_count, average_reconcile_backlog. Also add an SLO guard: if adaptive bursts let >Y% extra tokens in, page infra.
InfraBot: canary job created: `deploy enforcer:v2-adaptive` -> canary target orgs: org-canary-1, org-canary-2.
Amanda: rollout plan: 1) deploy read-only metrics + enable adaptive mode in monitor-only (no policy change) for 24h, 2) enable adaptive burst for canaries (2h), watch denies/latency/cost, 3) if stable, ramp to 5% of orgs, 4) full rollout + enable automatic reconciliation job nightly.
Josh: owners? Priya -> reconciliation job, Linus -> enforcement change, Carlo -> telemetry + alerting, Emma -> runbook & postmortem template. I'll coordinate canary.
Priya: one more note: make sure to add unit tests for backfill idempotency and reconcile markers so we never double-count.
Amanda: agreed. I'll open the RFC with config, prometheus queries, and rollout steps. tagging owners: @Priya @Linus @Carlo @Emma. :thumbsup:
Emma: thanks — I'll add runbook steps for on-call: how to quickly disable adaptive bursts and trigger immediate backfill if customer-impacting.
Josh: ok sounds good. if anything urgent, drop in #incidents.
InfraBot: alert cleared for enforcement-spike org-7f9.
Amanda: moving to action items, creating tasks in the board now.
